```{r}
# ENHANCED CORRELATION MATRIX
cat("Creating enhanced correlation matrix...\n")

# Select all numeric variables (excluding Real_T_canne and Surface_Age_days as requested)
excluded_vars <- c("Real_T_canne", "Surface_Age_days")

numeric_vars <- leaf_data_converted %>%
  select_if(is.numeric) %>%
  select(-any_of(excluded_vars))

# Remove variables that are entirely NA or have insufficient data for correlation
correlation_data <- numeric_vars %>%
  select_if(~ sum(!is.na(.)) > 10)  # Keep variables with at least 10 non-NA values

# Calculate correlation matrix with significance testing
cor_result <- rcorr(as.matrix(correlation_data), type = "pearson")
cor_matrix <- cor_result$r
p_matrix <- cor_result$P

# Handle any remaining NA/NaN/Inf values in correlation matrix
cor_matrix[is.na(cor_matrix)] <- 0
cor_matrix[is.infinite(cor_matrix)] <- 0

# Create enhanced correlation plot with BIGGER and BOLD fonts
png("Enhanced_Leaf_Boxplots_Publication/07_Enhanced_Correlation_Matrix.png", 
    width = 18, height = 16, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")

# Set up margins for title
par(mar = c(2, 2, 6, 3))

# Use standard blue to red color palette
corr_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#053061", "#2166AC", "#4393C3", "#92C5DE", 
                                 "#D1E5F0", "#F7F7F7", 
                                 "#FDDBC7", "#F4A582", "#D6604D", "#B2182B", "#67001F"))(100)

# Create the correlation plot with BIGGER and BOLD text
corrplot(cor_matrix,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         order = "original",
         col = corr_colors,
         tl.col = "#000000",
         tl.srt = 45,
         tl.cex = 1.2,         # BIGGER variable names
         tl.font = 2,          # BOLD variable names
         cl.cex = 1.3,         # BIGGER color legend text
         title = "Correlation Matrix of Leaf Dataset Variables\n(Excluding Real_T_canne and Surface_Age_days)",
         mar = c(0,0,4,0),
         diag = FALSE,
         addCoef.col = "#000000",
         number.cex = 0.7,     # BIGGER correlation values
         number.digits = 2,
         number.font = 2,      # BOLD correlation values
         outline = TRUE,
         cl.ratio = 0.2,
         cl.align.text = "c",
         cl.offset = 0.5)

# Add BIGGER and BOLDER significance stars
n_vars <- ncol(cor_matrix)
for(i in 1:(n_vars-1)) {
  for(j in (i+1):n_vars) {
    if(!is.na(p_matrix[i,j])) {
      if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.001) {
        sig_symbol <- "***"
        sig_color <- "#000000"
        sig_cex <- 1.0        # BIGGER significance stars
      } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.01) {
        sig_symbol <- "**"
        sig_color <- "#333333"
        sig_cex <- 1.0        # BIGGER significance stars
      } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.05) {
        sig_symbol <- "*"
        sig_color <- "#666666"
        sig_cex <- 1.0        # BIGGER significance stars
      } else {
        sig_symbol <- ""
        sig_color <- "black"
        sig_cex <- 1.0
      }
      
      if(sig_symbol != "") {
        x_center <- j
        y_center <- n_vars - i + 1
        text(x_center, y_center + 0.35, sig_symbol, 
             cex = sig_cex, col = sig_color, font = 2)  # BOLD significance stars
      }
    }
  }
}

# Enhanced legend with BIGGER text
legend_x <- n_vars * 0.7
legend_y <- n_vars * 0.9

legend(x = legend_x, y = legend_y,
       legend = c(
         "Statistical Significance:",
         "*** p < 0.001", 
         "**  p < 0.01", 
         "*   p < 0.05",
         "",
         "Correlation Strength:",
         "Red: Strong Positive (r > 0.7)",
         "Light Red: Moderate Positive (0.3 < r ≤ 0.7)", 
         "White: Weak (-0.3 ≤ r ≤ 0.3)",
         "Light Blue: Moderate Negative (-0.7 ≤ r < -0.3)",
         "Blue: Strong Negative (r < -0.7)"
       ), 
       text.col = c("#000000", "#000000", "#333333", "#666666", "white",
                   "#000000", "#B2182B", "#F4A582", "#000000", "#92C5DE", "#2166AC"), 
       bty = "n", 
       cex = 1.0,            # BIGGER legend text
       text.font = 2,        # BOLD legend text
       title = "Legend",
       title.col = "#000000",
       title.cex = 1.2,      # BIGGER legend title
       title.font = 2)       # BOLD legend title

dev.off()

# YIELD COMPARISON ANALYSIS
cat("Creating detailed yield comparison plots...\n")

# Scatter plot comparing yields with trend line
p_yield_scatter <- ggplot(leaf_data_converted, 
                         aes(x = Yield_tonnes_ha_year_minus_1, y = Yield_tonnes_ha_year_actual)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2, color = "#2F4F4F") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#DC143C", fill = "#FFB6C1", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#000000", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Yield Correlation: Current vs Previous Year",
    subtitle = "Red line shows trend, black dashed line shows perfect correlation",
    x = "Previous Year Yield (tonnes/ha)",
    y = "Current Year Yield (tonnes/ha)"
  ) +
  publication_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave("Enhanced_Leaf_Boxplots_Publication/08_Yield_Correlation_Scatter.png", p_yield_scatter,
       width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")  # Tighter dimensions

# Difference analysis
yield_diff_data <- leaf_data_converted %>%
  filter(!is.na(Yield_tonnes_ha_year_minus_1) & !is.na(Yield_tonnes_ha_year_actual)) %>%
  mutate(
    Yield_Difference = Yield_tonnes_ha_year_actual - Yield_tonnes_ha_year_minus_1,
    Yield_Percent_Change = (Yield_Difference / Yield_tonnes_ha_year_minus_1) * 100,
    Change_Category = case_when(
      Yield_Percent_Change > 10 ~ "Strong Increase (>10%)",
      Yield_Percent_Change > 0 ~ "Moderate Increase (0-10%)",
      Yield_Percent_Change >= -10 ~ "Moderate Decrease (0 to -10%)",
      TRUE ~ "Strong Decrease (<-10%)"
    )
  )

# Yield difference histogram
p_yield_diff <- ggplot(yield_diff_data, aes(x = Yield_Difference)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#4ECDC4", color = "#000000", alpha = 0.8, size = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#DC143C", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(yield_diff_data$Yield_Difference, na.rm = TRUE), 
             color = "#2F4F4F", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Yield Changes",
    subtitle = "Red line: no change, Dark line: mean change",
    x = "Yield Change (tonnes/ha)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  publication_theme

ggsave("Enhanced_Leaf_Boxplots_Publication/09_Yield_Difference_Distribution.png", p_yield_diff,
       width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")  # Tighter dimensions

# Summary statistics
cat("\n=== YIELD COMPARISON SUMMARY ===\n")
summary_stats <- yield_diff_data %>%
  summarise(
    n_observations = n(),
    mean_prev_yield = mean(Yield_tonnes_ha_year_minus_1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_curr_yield = mean(Yield_tonnes_ha_year_actual, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_difference = mean(Yield_Difference, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_percent_change = mean(Yield_Percent_Change, na.rm = TRUE),
    correlation = cor(Yield_tonnes_ha_year_minus_1, Yield_tonnes_ha_year_actual, use = "complete.obs")
  )

print(summary_stats)

# Category distribution
cat("\n=== YIELD CHANGE CATEGORIES ===\n")
category_summary <- yield_diff_data %>%
  count(Change_Category) %>%
  mutate(percentage = n / sum(n) * 100)

print(category_summary)
```

```{r}
# Enhanced publication-ready theme with TIGHT layout and narrow boxplots
publication_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12, family = "Arial", color = "#1C1C1C"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, color = "#000000", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "#333333", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#000000", margin = margin(t = 8)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#000000", margin = margin(r = 8)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, color = "#000000", angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, color = "#000000"),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#CCCCCC", size = 0.3, linetype = "solid"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "#000000", size = 0.8),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "#000000", size = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#000000"),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),  # Much tighter margins
    panel.spacing = unit(0.4, "lines"),    # Tighter panel spacing
    axis.line = element_line(color = "#000000", size = 0.6)
  )

# Function to detect outliers using IQR method
detect_outliers <- function(x) {
  q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
  return(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound)
}

# Enhanced function to create narrow boxplots with red outlier detection
create_enhanced_boxplot <- function(data_long, title, subtitle, colors, x_label, y_label, 
                                  variable_col = "variable", value_col = "value", remove_outliers = FALSE) {
  
  # Detect outliers for each variable
  data_with_outliers <- data_long %>%
    group_by(!!sym(variable_col)) %>%
    mutate(
      is_outlier = detect_outliers(!!sym(value_col)),
      outlier_label = ifelse(is_outlier, "Outlier", "Normal")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Remove outliers if requested
  if (remove_outliers) {
    plot_data <- data_with_outliers %>% filter(!is_outlier)
    title <- paste(title, "(Without Outliers)")
  } else {
    plot_data <- data_with_outliers
  }
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = variable_col, y = value_col, fill = variable_col)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      alpha = 0.85, 
      outlier.shape = NA,  # Hide default outliers
      width = 0.18,  # EVEN TIGHTER boxplots
      color = "#000000",  # Clear black contour
      size = 0.6,  # Slightly thinner for tighter look
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    # Add red outlier points manually
    {if (!remove_outliers) {
      geom_point(
        data = plot_data %>% filter(is_outlier),
        aes_string(x = variable_col, y = value_col),
        color = "#DC143C",  # Bright red for outliers
        size = 1.2,  # Slightly smaller for tighter layout
        alpha = 0.8,
        shape = 16,
        inherit.aes = FALSE
      )
    }} +
    stat_summary(
      fun = median, 
      geom = "text", 
      aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", after_stat(y))),
      size = 2.5,  # Slightly smaller text for tighter layout
      color = "white", 
      fontface = "bold",
      vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    publication_theme +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.01)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
  
  return(p)
}

         tl.font = 2,          # BOLD variable names
         cl.cex = 1.3,         # BIGGER color legend text
         title = "Correlation Matrix of Leaf Dataset Variables\n(Excluding Real_T_canne and Surface_Age_days)",
         mar = c(0,0,4,0),
         diag = FALSE,
         addCoef.col = "#000000",
         number.cex = 0.7,     # BIGGER correlation values
         number.digits = 2,
         number.font = 2,      # BOLD correlation values
         outline = TRUE,
         cl.ratio = 0.2,
         cl.align.text = "c",
         cl.offset = 0.5)

# Add BIGGER and BOLDER significance stars
n_vars <- ncol(cor_matrix)
for(i in 1:(n_vars-1)) {
  for(j in (i+1):n_vars) {
    if(!is.na(p_matrix[i,j])) {
      if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.001) {
        sig_symbol <- "***"
        sig_color <- "#000000"
        sig_cex <- 1.0        # BIGGER significance stars
      } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.01) {
        sig_symbol <- "**"
        sig_color <- "#333333"
        sig_cex <- 1.0        # BIGGER significance stars
      } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.05) {
        sig_symbol <- "*"
        sig_color <- "#666666"
        sig_cex <- 1.0        # BIGGER significance stars
      } else {
        sig_symbol <- ""
        sig_color <- "black"
        sig_cex <- 1.0
      }
      
      if(sig_symbol != "") {
        x_center <- j
        y_center <- n_vars - i + 1
        text(x_center, y_center + 0.35, sig_symbol, 
             cex = sig_cex, col = sig_color, font = 2)  # BOLD significance stars
      }
    }
  }
}

# Enhanced legend with BIGGER text

legend_y <- n_vars * 0.9

legend(

    "*   p < 0.05",
    "",
    "Correlation Strength:",
    "Red: Strong Positive (r > 0.7)",
    "Light Red: Moderate Positive (0.3 < r ≤ 0.7)", 
    "White: Weak (-0.3 ≤ r ≤ 0.3)",
    "Light Blue: Moderate Negative (-0.7 ≤ r < -0.3)",
    "Blue: Strong Negative (r < -0.7)"
  ),

  bty = "n",
  cex = 1.0,

# Enhanced theme for categorical comparisons with legend
categorical_theme <- publication_theme +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.margin = margin(t = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, color = "#000000", angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),  # No angle for categories
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "#000000")
  )

# Function for categorical boxplots with AUTOMATIC color generation
create_categorical_boxplot <- function(data, y_var, group_var, title, subtitle, y_label, group_label, colors = NULL) {
  
  # Filter out NA values
  plot_data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(y_var)) & !is.na(!!sym(group_var)) & !!sym(group_var) != "")
  
  # Get unique groups and count them
  unique_groups <- unique(plot_data[[group_var]])
  n_groups <- length(unique_groups)
  
  # Create color palette automatically based on number of groups
  if(is.null(colors) || length(colors) < n_groups) {
    if(n_groups <= 16) {
      # Use predefined colors for smaller groups
      colors <- publication_colors$comparison_colors[1:n_groups]
    } else {
      # Generate colors automatically for larger groups
      if(n_groups <= 30) {
        # Use RColorBrewer for medium groups
        colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(min(n_groups, 11), "Spectral")
        if(n_groups > 11) {
          colors <- colorRampPalette(colors)(n_groups)
        }
      } else {
        # Use viridis for very large groups
        colors <- viridis::viridis(n_groups, alpha = 0.8)
      }
    }
  } else {
    # Extend provided colors if needed
    if(length(colors) < n_groups) {
      colors <- colorRampPalette(colors)(n_groups)
    }
  }
  
  # Ensure we have exactly the right number of colors
  colors <- colors[1:n_groups]
  
  cat("Creating plot for", n_groups, "groups in", group_var, "\n")
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = group_var, y = y_var, fill = group_var)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      alpha = 0.85,
      outlier.shape = NA,
      width = 0.6,  # Wider for categorical comparisons
      color = "#000000",
      size = 0.6,
      show.legend = ifelse(n_groups > 10, FALSE, TRUE)  # Hide legend if too many groups
    ) +
    geom_point(
      position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0),
      alpha = 0.4,
      size = 0.8,
      color = "#333333",
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    stat_summary(
      fun = median,
      geom = "text",
      aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", after_stat(y))),
      size = ifelse(n_groups > 15, 2.0, 2.5),  # Smaller text for many groups
      color = "white",
      fontface = "bold",
      vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors, name = group_label) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = paste(subtitle, "(", n_groups, "groups)"),
      x = group_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    categorical_theme +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.01)) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = ifelse(n_groups > 8, 45, 0), 
        hjust = ifelse(n_groups > 8, 1, 0.5),
        size = ifelse(n_groups > 15, 7, 9)  # Smaller text for many groups
      ),
      legend.position = ifelse(n_groups > 10, "none", "bottom")
    )
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to create statistical summary
create_categorical_summary <- function(data, numeric_var, category_var) {
  if(all(c(numeric_var, category_var) %in% names(data))) {
    summary_table <- data %>%
      filter(!is.na(!!sym(numeric_var)) & !is.na(!!sym(category_var)) & !!sym(category_var) != "") %>%
      group_by(!!sym(category_var)) %>%
      summarise(
        n = n(),
        mean = round(mean(!!sym(numeric_var), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
        median = round(median(!!sym(numeric_var), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
        sd = round(sd(!!sym(numeric_var), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
        min = round(min(!!sym(numeric_var), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
        max = round(max(!!sym(numeric_var), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
        .groups = 'drop'
      ) %>%
      arrange(desc(mean))
    
    cat(paste("\n=== SUMMARY:", numeric_var, "BY", category_var, "===\n"))
    print(summary_table)
    return(summary_table)
  }
}

# Generate summaries for key comparisons

  create_categorical_summary(leaf_data_converted, "Leaf_Moisture_percent", "Variety")
}

}

if("Irrigation_Type" %in% names(leaf_data_converted)) {

}
```

# V. Multivariate Data Analysis - PCA

```{r}
# Multivariate Data Analysis for Sugar Cane Leaf Dataset using explor package
# Load required libraries
library(explor)
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(corrplot)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(RColorBrewer)

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("MULTIVARIATE DATA ANALYSIS - SUGAR CANE LEAF DATASET\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Prepare the data for multivariate analysis
cat("Preparing leaf data for multivariate analysis...\n")

cat("• Total rows in leaf_data_converted:", nrow(leaf_data_converted), "\n")
cat("• Total columns:", ncol(leaf_data_converted), "\n")
cat("• Column names:", paste(names(leaf_data_converted)[1:min(10, ncol(leaf_data_converted))], collapse = ", "), "...\n\n")

# Get all numeric variables, excluding ID-like variables and previously excluded ones
excluded_vars <- c("Real_T_canne", "Surface_Age_days", "Plot", "Campaign", 
                   "Farm", "Variety", "Crop_Cycle", "Growth_Period",
                   "Irrigation_Type", "Harvest_Month", "Sampling_Month", 
                   "Week_Number", "Data_Day", "Period_Validation", 
                   "Plot_Campaign", "Harvest_Validation", "Note")

numeric_vars <- leaf_data_converted %>%
  select_if(is.numeric) %>%
  select(-any_of(excluded_vars)) %>%
  names()

cat("Identified numeric variables:", length(numeric_vars), "\n")
if(length(numeric_vars) > 0) {
  cat("Variables for PCA:\n")
  for(i in 1:length(numeric_vars)) {
    cat("  ", i, ". ", numeric_vars[i], "\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("ERROR: No numeric variables found!\n")
  stop("Please check your data structure")
}

# Check for missing values in each variable
missing_summary <- leaf_data_converted %>%
  select(all_of(numeric_vars)) %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(is.na(.))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing_count") %>%
  mutate(missing_percent = round(missing_count / nrow(leaf_data_converted) * 100, 2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))

cat("\nMissing values summary:\n")
print(missing_summary)

# Remove variables with too many missing values (>70% for leaf data)
vars_to_keep <- missing_summary %>%
  filter(missing_percent <= 70) %>%
  pull(variable)

cat("\nKeeping", length(vars_to_keep), "variables with ≤70% missing values\n")
cat("Variables kept:", paste(vars_to_keep, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Variables removed due to high missingness
vars_removed <- missing_summary %>%
  filter(missing_percent > 70) %>%
  pull(variable)

if(length(vars_removed) > 0) {
  cat("Variables removed due to >70% missing:", paste(vars_removed, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

# Create analysis dataset with categorical info for supplementary analysis
categorical_vars <- c("Campaign", "Farm", "Variety", "Crop_Cycle", "Growth_Period", "Irrigation_Type")
existing_categorical <- intersect(categorical_vars, names(leaf_data_converted))

analysis_data <- leaf_data_converted %>%
  select(all_of(vars_to_keep), any_of(existing_categorical))

# Remove rows with too many missing values (>50% of numeric variables)
numeric_data_for_filtering <- analysis_data %>% select(all_of(vars_to_keep))
rows_to_keep <- rowSums(is.na(numeric_data_for_filtering)) <= length(vars_to_keep) * 0.5

analysis_data <- analysis_data[rows_to_keep, ]

cat("\nAfter filtering:\n")
cat("• Numeric variables:", length(vars_to_keep), "\n")
cat("• Categorical variables:", length(existing_categorical), "\n")
cat("• Observations:", nrow(analysis_data), "\n\n")

if(nrow(analysis_data) == 0) {
  stop("ERROR: No observations left after filtering!")
}

# Extract numeric data for PCA and handle remaining missing values
pca_data <- analysis_data %>%
  select(all_of(vars_to_keep))

# Replace remaining missing values with column medians (more robust for agricultural data)
pca_data <- pca_data %>%
  mutate_all(~ifelse(is.na(.), median(., na.rm = TRUE), .))

# Check for and remove variables with zero variance
var_check <- apply(pca_data, 2, function(x) {
  if(all(is.na(x))) {
    return(NA)
  } else {
    return(var(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
})

# Identify problematic columns
zero_var_cols <- names(var_check)[var_check == 0 | is.na(var_check) | is.infinite(var_check)]

if(length(zero_var_cols) > 0) {
  cat("Removing", length(zero_var_cols), "variables with zero/NA/infinite variance:\n")
  cat(paste(zero_var_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
  pca_data <- pca_data %>% select(-all_of(zero_var_cols))
  vars_to_keep <- setdiff(vars_to_keep, zero_var_cols)
} else {
  cat("All variables have valid variance.\n\n")
}

# Scale the data (important for PCA when variables have different units)
pca_data_scaled <- scale(pca_data)

# Add meaningful rownames
if("Campaign" %in% names(analysis_data) && "Plot" %in% names(leaf_data_converted)) {
  rownames(pca_data_scaled) <- paste0("Obs_", 1:nrow(pca_data_scaled))
} else {
  rownames(pca_data_scaled) <- paste0("Sample_", 1:nrow(pca_data_scaled))
}

# Update final variables
numeric_vars_final <- vars_to_keep

cat("Final dataset for PCA:\n")
cat("• Variables:", ncol(pca_data_scaled), "\n")
cat("• Observations:", nrow(pca_data_scaled), "\n")
cat("• Final variables:", paste(numeric_vars_final, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

# Create output directory
if(!dir.exists("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis")) {
  dir.create("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis", recursive = TRUE)
}

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("1. PRINCIPAL COMPONENT ANALYSIS (PCA)\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Perform PCA using FactoMineR
# Include supplementary categorical variables if available
if(length(existing_categorical) > 0) {
  # Prepare supplementary qualitative variables
  sup_data <- analysis_data %>% 
    select(all_of(existing_categorical)) %>%
    mutate_all(as.factor)
  
  # Remove rows with all NA in supplementary variables
  sup_data[is.na(sup_data)] <- "Unknown"
  
  # Find columns in supplementary data
  sup_quali <- which(names(analysis_data) %in% existing_categorical)
  
  cat("Including supplementary categorical variables:", paste(existing_categorical, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  
  pca_result <- PCA(
    cbind(pca_data_scaled, sup_data), 
    scale.unit = FALSE,  # Already scaled
    quali.sup = sup_quali,  # Supplementary qualitative variables
    graph = FALSE,       # Don't show default plots
    ncp = min(10, ncol(pca_data_scaled))  # Max 10 components
  )
} else {
  cat("No supplementary categorical variables found\n")
  pca_result <- PCA(pca_data_scaled, 
                    scale.unit = FALSE,
                    graph = FALSE,
                    ncp = min(10, ncol(pca_data_scaled)))
}

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("2. INTERACTIVE PCA EXPLORATION\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Note: This will open an interactive Shiny app
# Uncomment the line below to launch the interactive explorer
explor(pca_result)

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("3. CORRELATION ANALYSIS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Create correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(pca_data, use = "complete.obs")

# Enhanced correlation plot
png("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/correlation_matrix.png", 
    width = 14, height = 12, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")

par(mar = c(2, 2, 4, 2))
corrplot(cor_matrix, 
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         order = "hclust",
         tl.col = "#000000",
         tl.srt = 45,
         tl.cex = 1.0,
         tl.font = 2,
         cl.cex = 1.1,
         col = colorRampPalette(c("#053061", "#2166AC", "#4393C3", "#92C5DE", 
                                 "#D1E5F0", "#F7F7F7", 
                                 "#FDDBC7", "#F4A582", "#D6604D", "#B2182B", "#67001F"))(100),
         title = "Sugar Cane Leaf Dataset - Correlation Matrix\n",
         mar = c(0,0,3,0),
         diag = FALSE,
         addCoef.col = "#000000",
         number.cex = 0.6,
         number.digits = 2,
         outline = TRUE)

dev.off()

cat("Correlation matrix saved as correlation_matrix.png\n\n")

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("4. PCA SUMMARY STATISTICS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Print PCA summary
cat("Eigenvalues and variance explained:\n")
eigen_summary <- round(pca_result$eig, 3)
print(eigen_summary)

# Calculate how many components explain 80% of variance
cum_var <- pca_result$eig[,3]
components_80 <- which(cum_var >= 80)[1]
cat("\nComponents needed to explain 80% variance:", components_80, "\n")

cat("\nVariables with highest contributions to PC1:\n")
contrib_pc1 <- sort(pca_result$var$contrib[,1], decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(10, nrow(pca_result$var$contrib))]
print(round(contrib_pc1, 2))

cat("\nVariables with highest contributions to PC2:\n")
contrib_pc2 <- sort(pca_result$var$contrib[,2], decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(10, nrow(pca_result$var$contrib))]
print(round(contrib_pc2, 2))

cat("\nVariables with highest quality of representation (Cos2) on PC1-PC2:\n")
cos2_pc12 <- pca_result$var$cos2[,1] + pca_result$var$cos2[,2]
best_represented <- sort(cos2_pc12, decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(10, length(cos2_pc12))]
print(round(best_represented, 3))

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("5. DETAILED PCA VISUALIZATIONS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# 1. Enhanced scree plot
scree_plot <- fviz_eig(pca_result, 
                       addlabels = TRUE, 
                       ylim = c(0, max(pca_result$eig[,2]) * 1.1),
                       barfill = "#4ECDC4",
                       barcolor = "#2F4F4F",
                       linecolor = "#DC143C") +
  ggtitle("PCA Scree Plot - Sugar Cane Leaf Dataset") +
  labs(subtitle = paste("First", components_80, "components explain 80% of variance")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

ggsave("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/pca_scree_plot.png", scree_plot,
       width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# 2. Enhanced biplot
biplot <- fviz_pca_biplot(pca_result, 
                         repel = TRUE,
                         col.var = "#2E9FDF",
                         col.ind = "#696969",
                         alpha.ind = 0.3,
                         alpha.var = 0.8,
                         title = "PCA Biplot - Sugar Cane Leaf Variables and Observations",
                         subtitle = paste("PC1 (", round(pca_result$eig[1,2], 1), "%) vs PC2 (", 
                                        round(pca_result$eig[2,2], 1), "%)", sep="")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))

ggsave("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/pca_biplot.png", biplot,
       width = 12, height = 9, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# 3. Variables contribution plot
var_plot <- fviz_pca_var(pca_result,
                        col.var = "contrib",
                        gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"),
                        repel = TRUE,
                        title = "Variables Contribution to PC1-PC2",
                        subtitle = "Color intensity = Contribution level") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))

ggsave("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/pca_variables_plot.png", var_plot,
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# 4. Variables quality plot (cos2)
cos2_plot <- fviz_pca_var(pca_result,
                         col.var = "cos2",
                         gradient.cols = c("#BB4444", "#EE9988", "#FFFFFF", "#77AADD", "#4477AA"),
                         repel = TRUE,
                         title = "Variables Quality of Representation (Cos2)",
                         subtitle = "How well variables are represented by PC1-PC2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))

ggsave("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/pca_variables_cos2_plot.png", cos2_plot,
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# 5. Individuals plot colored by contribution
ind_plot <- fviz_pca_ind(pca_result,
                        col.ind = "contrib",
                        gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"),
                        repel = FALSE,
                        alpha.ind = 0.6,
                        title = "Individuals Plot - Colored by Contribution",
                        subtitle = "Each point represents one observation") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))

ggsave("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/pca_individuals_plot.png", ind_plot,
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("6. SUPPLEMENTARY CATEGORICAL ANALYSIS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Analyze supplementary categorical variables if available
if(length(existing_categorical) > 0) {
  for(cat_var in existing_categorical) {
    if(cat_var %in% names(analysis_data)) {
      cat("Analyzing", cat_var, "...\n")
      
      # Create plot colored by categorical variable
      cat_levels <- unique(analysis_data[[cat_var]])
      cat_levels <- cat_levels[!is.na(cat_levels) & cat_levels != ""]
      
      if(length(cat_levels) > 1 && length(cat_levels) <= 20) {
        # Create color palette
        if(length(cat_levels) <= 8) {
          colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(max(3, length(cat_levels)), "Set2")[1:length(cat_levels)]
        } else {
          colors <- rainbow(length(cat_levels))
        }
        
        # Plot individuals colored by categorical variable
        tryCatch({
          sup_plot <- fviz_pca_ind(pca_result,
                                  habillage = cat_var,
                                  palette = colors,
                                  addEllipses = TRUE,
                                  ellipse.level = 0.68,
                                  repel = FALSE,
                                  alpha.ind = 0.7,
                                  title = paste("PCA - Individuals colored by", cat_var),
                                  subtitle = paste("Ellipses show 68% confidence intervals")) +
            theme_minimal() +
            theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11),
                  legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
          
          filename <- paste0("Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/pca_by_", tolower(cat_var), ".png")
          ggsave(filename, sup_plot, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
          
          cat("  • Saved:", filename, "\n")
        }, error = function(e) {
          cat("  • Could not create plot for", cat_var, ":", e$message, "\n")
        })
      } else {
        cat("  • Skipping", cat_var, "- too many levels or insufficient data\n")
      }
    }
  }
}

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("7. AGRICULTURAL INTERPRETATION ANALYSIS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Group variables by agricultural meaning
agricultural_groups <- list(
  Yield = grep("yield|Yield", numeric_vars_final, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Moisture = grep("moisture|Moisture", numeric_vars_final, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Nutrients = grep("nitrogen|phosphorus|potassium|Nitrogen|Phosphorus|Potassium", numeric_vars_final, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Age = grep("age|Age|weeks|Weeks", numeric_vars_final, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Surface = grep("surface|Surface|ha", numeric_vars_final, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Sugar = grep("pol|sugar|Sugar|T_", numeric_vars_final, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
)

# Remove empty groups
agricultural_groups <- agricultural_groups[sapply(agricultural_groups, length) > 0]

cat("Variable groups identified:\n")
for(group_name in names(agricultural_groups)) {
  cat("•", group_name, ":", length(agricultural_groups[[group_name]]), "variables\n")
  cat("  Variables:", paste(agricultural_groups[[group_name]], collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

# Create contribution analysis by groups
cat("\nContribution of variable groups to first 3 PCs:\n")
for(i in 1:min(3, ncol(pca_result$var$contrib))) {
  cat("\n--- PC", i, "(", round(pca_result$eig[i,2], 1), "% variance) ---\n")
  
  for(group_name in names(agricultural_groups)) {
    group_vars <- agricultural_groups[[group_name]]
    group_contrib <- sum(pca_result$var$contrib[group_vars, i], na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(group_name, "group total contribution:", round(group_contrib, 2), "%\n")
  }
}

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("8. SAVE COMPREHENSIVE RESULTS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Save all PCA results
save(pca_result, pca_data, pca_data_scaled, cor_matrix, 
     agricultural_groups, analysis_data, numeric_vars_final,
     file = "Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/leaf_pca_complete_results.RData")

# Create comprehensive summary table
n_components <- min(10, nrow(pca_result$eig))
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Component = paste0("PC", 1:n_components),
  Eigenvalue = round(pca_result$eig[1:n_components, 1], 3),
  Variance_Percent = round(pca_result$eig[1:n_components, 2], 2),
  Cumulative_Percent = round(pca_result$eig[1:n_components, 3], 2)
)

write.csv(summary_table, "Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/pca_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create variable contributions table
contrib_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(pca_result$var$contrib),
  PC1_Contrib = round(pca_result$var$contrib[,1], 3),
  PC2_Contrib = round(pca_result$var$contrib[,2], 3),
  PC3_Contrib = round(pca_result$var$contrib[,3], 3),
  PC1_Cos2 = round(pca_result$var$cos2[,1], 3),
  PC2_Cos2 = round(pca_result$var$cos2[,2], 3),
  PC3_Cos2 = round(pca_result$var$cos2[,3], 3)
)

write.csv(contrib_table, "Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/variables_contributions.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create coordinates table for individuals
coord_table <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(pca_result$ind$coord),
  PC1 = round(pca_result$ind$coord[,1], 3),
  PC2 = round(pca_result$ind$coord[,2], 3),
  PC3 = round(pca_result$ind$coord[,3], 3)
)

# Add categorical information if available
if(length(existing_categorical) > 0) {
  for(cat_var in existing_categorical) {
    if(cat_var %in% names(analysis_data)) {
      coord_table[[cat_var]] <- analysis_data[[cat_var]]
    }
  }
}

write.csv(coord_table, "Enhanced_Leaf_PCA_Analysis/sample_coordinates.csv", row.names = FALSE)


cat("explor(pca_result)\n\n")

# Summary statistics
cat("FINAL DATASET SUMMARY:\n")
cat("• Original variables:", length(numeric_vars), "\n")
cat("• Variables after filtering:", length(numeric_vars_final), "\n")
cat("• Final observations:", nrow(pca_data_scaled), "\n")
cat("• Categorical variables included:", length(existing_categorical), "\n")
cat("• Components explaining 80% variance:", components_80, "\n")

```

```{r}
# 3x3 PCA Variables Plot Grid 
# Load required libraries
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(cowplot)
library(dplyr)

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("3x3 PCA VARIABLES PLOT GRID - ALL VARIABLES VISIBLE\n")
cat("SUGAR CANE LEAF DATASET - UNIFORM SIZING\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Check if PCA result exists
if(!exists("pca_result")) {
  stop("ERROR: pca_result not found. Please run the PCA analysis first!")
}

# Define sophisticated color palettes for agricultural data
agricultural_colors <- c("#228B22", "#32CD32", "#FF6347", "#FFD700", "#87CEEB", "#DDA0DD", "#F4A460", "#98FB98", "#FF69B4")

# Create custom theme for bold, professional plots with UNIFORM sizing
theme_pca_agricultural <- function() {
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # UNIFORM TEXT SIZING FOR AGRICULTURAL DATA
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, color = "#1B4332", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "#52796F", margin = margin(b = 6)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "#2D6A4F"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "#1B4332"),
    
    # UNIFORM LEGEND STYLING
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", color = "#1B4332", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "#1B4332"),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.45, "cm"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 8),
    legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    
    # AGRICULTURAL-THEMED GRID AND BACKGROUND
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#E8F5E8", size = 0.4, linetype = "dashed"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "#F0FFF0", size = 0.25, linetype = "dotted"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FEFFFE", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    
    # UNIFORM LEGEND BACKGROUND
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#F8FFF8", color = "#95D5B2", size = 0.4),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    
    # UNIFORM MARGINS
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
    
    # STRIP TEXT FOR MULTI-PANEL CONSISTENCY
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, color = "#1B4332"),
    
    # ENSURE SQUARE ASPECT RATIO
    aspect.ratio = 1
  )
}

# Enhanced function to create PCA variable plot showing ALL variables
create_agricultural_pca_plot <- function(pca_result, axes = c(1, 2), plot_title = "", 
                                         color_type = "contrib") {
  
  # Check if axes exist
  if (max(axes) > ncol(pca_result$var$coord)) {
    return(create_placeholder_plot(plot_title, axes))
  }
  
  # Variance explained for axis labels
  var_exp_1 <- round(pca_result$eig[axes[1], 2], 1)
  var_exp_2 <- round(pca_result$eig[axes[2], 2], 1)
  
  # --- CASE 1: Contribution ---
  if (color_type == "contrib") {
    p <- fviz_pca_var(pca_result,
                      axes = axes,
                      col.var = "contrib",
                      alpha.var = 0.85,
                      repel = TRUE,
                      labelsize = 3.0,
                      pointsize = 2.2,
                      arrowsize = 0.7,
                      select.var = list(contrib = Inf)) +  # Show ALL variables
      scale_color_gradient2(low = "#2D6A4F", mid = "#F77F00", high = "#D62828",
                            midpoint = 50, name = "Contrib\n%",
                            guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", 
                                                   title.hjust = 0.5,
                                                   barwidth = 1.3,
                                                   barheight = 5.0,
                                                   ticks.colour = "#1B4332",
                                                   ticks.linewidth = 0.6,
                                                   frame.colour = "#1B4332",
                                                   frame.linewidth = 0.8)) +
      labs(title = plot_title,
           subtitle = paste0("PC", axes[1], " & PC", axes[2], " • All Variables"),
           x = paste0("PC", axes[1], " (", var_exp_1, "% variance)"),
           y = paste0("PC", axes[2], " (", var_exp_2, "% variance)"))
    
  # --- CASE 2: Cos² quality ---
  } else if (color_type == "cos2") {
    p <- fviz_pca_var(pca_result,
                      axes = axes,
                      col.var = "cos2",
                      alpha.var = 0.85,
                      repel = TRUE,
                      labelsize = 3.0,
                      pointsize = 2.2,
                      arrowsize = 0.7,
                      select.var = list(cos2 = 0)) +  # Show ALL variables
      scale_color_viridis_c(option = "viridis", name = "Quality\n(Cos²)",
                            guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", 
                                                   title.hjust = 0.5,
                                                   barwidth = 1.3,
                                                   barheight = 5.0,
                                                   ticks.colour = "#1B4332",
                                                   ticks.linewidth = 0.6,
                                                   frame.colour = "#1B4332",
                                                   frame.linewidth = 0.8)) +
      labs(title = plot_title,
           subtitle = paste0("PC", axes[1], " & PC", axes[2], " • All Variables"),
           x = paste0("PC", axes[1], " (", var_exp_1, "% variance)"),
           y = paste0("PC", axes[2], " (", var_exp_2, "% variance)"))
  }
  
  # Apply agricultural theme
  p <- p + theme_pca_agricultural()
  
  # Add reference lines, border, and fixed square ratio
  p <- p +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "#52796F", size = 0.9, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "#52796F", size = 0.9, alpha = 0.8) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = NA, color = "#1B4332", size = 1.3) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1,
                xlim = c(-1.1, 1.1),
                ylim = c(-1.1, 1.1),
                expand = FALSE,
                clip = "on")
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to create placeholder plot for missing dimensions
create_placeholder_plot <- function(title, axes) {
  ggplot() + 
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, 
             label = paste("PC", max(axes), "\nnot available\nin dataset"), 
             size = 5, color = "#52796F", fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = -0.3,
             label = "Insufficient components\nfor this combination",
             size = 3.5, color = "#7F8C8D") +
    labs(title = title, 
         subtitle = paste0("PC", axes[1], " & PC", axes[2], " • Not Available")) +
    theme_pca_agricultural() +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), 
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank()) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1))
}

# Define the 9 different dimension combinations
plot_combinations <- list(
  list(axes = c(1, 2), title = "Primary Components", color = "contrib"),
  list(axes = c(1, 3), title = "Main vs Third", color = "cos2"),
  list(axes = c(2, 3), title = "Secondary vs Third", color = "contrib"),
  list(axes = c(1, 4), title = "Primary Extended", color = "cos2"),
  list(axes = c(2, 4), title = "Secondary Extended", color = "contrib"),
  list(axes = c(3, 4), title = "Middle Components", color = "cos2"),
  list(axes = c(1, 5), title = "Primary vs Fifth", color = "contrib"),
  list(axes = c(2, 5), title = "Secondary vs Fifth", color = "cos2"),
  list(axes = c(3, 5), title = "Tertiary vs Fifth", color = "contrib")
)

# Create individual plots showing ALL variables
cat("Creating individual PCA variable plots showing ALL variables...\n")
plot_list <- list()

for(i in 1:9) {
  combo <- plot_combinations[[i]]
  
  cat("Creating plot", i, ":", combo$title, "(", paste(combo$axes, collapse=" vs "), ") with", combo$color, "coloring...\n")
  
  plot_list[[i]] <- create_agricultural_pca_plot(pca_result, 
                                               axes = combo$axes, 
                                               plot_title = combo$title,
                                               color_type = combo$color)
}

cat("All 9 plots created successfully!\n\n")

# Create the 3x3 grid layout
cat("Arranging plots in 3x3 grid...\n")

# Create main title
main_title <- ggdraw() + 
  draw_label("Sugar Cane Leaf Dataset: PCA Variables Grid - All Variables Shown", 
             fontface = 'bold', size = 18, color = "#1B4332") +
  draw_label("Complete visualization of all variable loadings across multiple PC dimensions", 
             fontface = 'plain', size = 12, color = "#52796F", 
             x = 0.5, y = 0.25) +
  draw_label("No variables filtered - all displayed in each plot", 
             fontface = 'italic', size = 10, color = "#74A57F", 
             x = 0.5, y = 0.05) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA))

# Arrange plots in 3x3 grid
variables_grid <- plot_grid(
  plot_list[[1]], plot_list[[2]], plot_list[[3]],
  plot_list[[4]], plot_list[[5]], plot_list[[6]],
  plot_list[[7]], plot_list[[8]], plot_list[[9]],
  ncol = 3, nrow = 3,
  align = "hv",
  axis = "tblr",
  rel_widths = c(1, 1, 1),
  rel_heights = c(1, 1, 1),
  hjust = 0.5,
  vjust = 0.5,
  scale = 0.96
)

# Combine title with grid
final_plot <- plot_grid(
  main_title, 
  variables_grid,
  ncol = 1,
  rel_heights = c(0.08, 0.92),
  align = "hv"
)

# Create output directory
if(!dir.exists("PCA_Analysis_All_Variables")) {
  dir.create("PCA_Analysis_All_Variables", recursive = TRUE)
}

# Save the comprehensive plot
cat("Saving comprehensive 3x3 PCA variables grid (all variables)...\n")

# High-resolution version
ggsave("PCA_Analysis_All_Variables/pca_variables_3x3_grid_all_variables.png", 
       final_plot,
       width = 20, height = 20,
       dpi = 300, 
       bg = "white",
       device = "png")

# Medium resolution version
ggsave("PCA_Analysis_All_Variables/pca_variables_3x3_grid_medium.png", 
       final_plot,
       width = 16, height = 16,
       dpi = 200, 
       bg = "white",
       device = "png")


# Print variable information
if(exists("pca_result")) {
  cat("VARIABLES INCLUDED IN ANALYSIS:\n")
  var_names <- rownames(pca_result$var$coord)
  for(i in 1:length(var_names)) {
    cat(sprintf("%2d. %s\n", i, var_names[i]))
  }
  
  cat("\nPCA DIMENSIONS AVAILABLE:", ncol(pca_result$var$coord), "\n")
  cat("VARIANCE EXPLAINED BY FIRST 5 PCs:\n")
  first_5 <- min(5, nrow(pca_result$eig))
  for(i in 1:first_5) {
    cat(sprintf("PC%d: %.1f%% (cumulative: %.1f%%)\n", 
                i, pca_result$eig[i,2], pca_result$eig[i,3]))
  }
}
```
